stemMd: Although the museum's new wing was designed to be ______, its glass walls and soaring atrium so overwhelm the row of modest brick houses beside it that visitors notice the building before they notice anything else on the street.
instructionsMd: Select one entry for the blank from the corresponding column of choices. Fill the blank in the way that best completes the text.
explanationMd:
Single-blank Text Completion is decided by structure before vocabulary, so find the connector first.

**Step 1 — read the signal word.** The sentence opens with **"Although,"** which announces that the two halves of the sentence will conflict. Whatever fills the blank must therefore be the *opposite* of what the second half describes.

**Step 2 — read what the second half actually says.** The glass walls and soaring atrium "overwhelm" the neighbouring houses, and visitors notice the building first. That is a description of a building that draws attention to itself and dominates its street.

**Step 3 — predict, then match.** The designers intended the opposite: a building that does *not* draw attention, that blends in. **"Unobtrusive"** — not pushing itself on the notice of others — is exactly that prediction, so the answer is (B).

**How to check.** Read the completed sentence aloud and test whether the "although" is earning its place: *designed to be unobtrusive, yet it dominates the street.* The contrast is real, so the connector is satisfied. Apply the same test to any choice you were tempted by; if the sentence reads just as well with "and" as with "although," you have almost certainly picked the wrong word, because a contrast connector demands an actual reversal.

distractorRationale.c: "Assertive" describes a building that does insist on being noticed, which is what the second half of the sentence says the wing actually does. Choosing it turns the contrast signalled by "although" into an agreement, so the connector no longer makes sense.
distractorRationale.e: "Ornamental" means decorative. A decorative building can perfectly well dominate its neighbours, so this word creates no tension with the glass walls and soaring atrium and leaves "although" with nothing to contrast.
distractorRationale.d: "Symmetrical" describes the balance of a design, a property entirely unrelated to whether a building overwhelms the houses next to it. Nothing in the sentence concerns the arrangement of the wing's parts.
distractorRationale.a: "Provisional" means temporary or intended to be replaced. The sentence says nothing about how long the wing is meant to stand, and a temporary structure could be just as conspicuous as a permanent one.

accessibilityText: A sentence with one blank. Although the museum's new wing was designed to be blank, its glass walls and soaring atrium so overwhelm the row of modest brick houses beside it that visitors notice the building before they notice anything else on the street. The five choices are: A, assertive. B, unobtrusive. C, ornamental. D, symmetrical. E, provisional. Select one entry for the blank.

provenance.notes: Original single-blank Text Completion written for the wave 3 top-up. The contrast connector 'although' and the explicit consequence clause together fix one answer; each distractor fails a different part of that structure. Not adapted from any ETS item.

independentSolve.workingNotes: 'Although' sets the blank against the result that the wing overwhelms its neighbours and is the first thing visitors notice; the intended design must therefore have been unobtrusive. Assertive matches the outcome rather than contrasting with it, and provisional, symmetrical and ornamental are not negated by the second clause.

review.notes: Author solved as B: 'although' demands the reverse of a building that overwhelms its neighbours, so the intended quality is unobtrusiveness. Uniqueness: assertive reverses the contrast, ornamental and symmetrical are compatible with dominating the street, and provisional concerns duration rather than prominence.
